html:
The control problem (reactive  100-300 ms orienting vs proactive, sustained control over seconds-to-minutes); what do we mean by control? It is distinguished from reflexive actions right?

Define the "triple-network" roles up front: Salience (aINS-dACC) detects control-worthy events and triggers switching; FPCN/MD implements top-down control and couples flexibly to either DAN (for externally oriented tasks) or DMN (for model-based, internal simulation); DMN supplies latent-model priors and prospective simulation that FPCN can harness when tasks demand abstraction

Unify the computational lens so each section answers the same questions: what variables are represented (e.g., priority maps, latent task state, expected value of control, uncertainty/precision), what operations are performed on them (gain modulation, gating, arbitChecration, policy compilation), and what dynamics implement those operations (bursting regimes, coherence patterns, neuromodulatory state).

The brain’s control systems are characterized by hierarchical organization and dynamic reconfiguration

The SN decides when to reroute resources, the DAN/VAN decide where to look next, and the CEN/FPN decides what to do with the information once it arrives; SN relevance approximator, DAN/VAN spotlight operators, CEN/FPN central executive

Salience network operates on macroscopic brain states; can switch from exogenous to endogenous perception, for instance

PFC

Collection of hierarchical models that provide goal-directed abstractions over tasks and semantics

Integrates information from across the brain; brings it all together

Can be seen as a map 1 and orchestrator of the brain
